questions.q: Where can you see the Northern Lights in the UK?
questions.answer: In the UK, the Northern Lights can be seen in northern areas of the British Isles, including the Hebrides in Scotland, especially the Outer Hebrides on the islands of Lewis or Harris.

questions.q: What is the best place to see the Northern Lights in the Hebrides?
questions.answer: The best bet for seeing the Northern Lights in the Hebrides is the Outer Hebrides, likely on the islands of Lewis or Harris.

questions.q: When is the Northern Lights season in the Hebrides?
questions.answer: The Northern Lights season in the Hebrides runs from September to April, though the aurora is most common in winter.

questions.q: What festival takes place on the Isle of Lewis in February?
questions.answer: The Isle of Lewis hosts its own Dark Skies Festival in February, with events including live music, film and theatre.

questions.q: What celestial objects can be seen from the Hebrides?
questions.answer: From the Hebrides, you may see the Orion Nebula, the Milky Way and the Great Andromeda galaxy.

questions.q: What are the viewing conditions for the Northern Lights in the Outer Hebrides?
questions.answer: The Outer Hebrides have flat beaches and countryside that are great viewing points, with remote parts subject to almost no light pollution and exceptionally dark skies.
